# Install from a fresh Mac

Start here if you have never installed Neovim, Homebrew, or a terminal development tool. Follow the steps in order. No GitHub or AI account is needed for the local practice workspace.

[Interactive guide / Panduan interaktif](https://ardanngrha.github.io/vimdesk/?lang=en#install)

Mac-first guide. Neovim 0.12+ and Python 3.9+ are required. Linux has not been validated end to end; Windows is unsupported.

## 1. Open Terminal

Press Command + Space, type Terminal, then press Enter. This guide uses the default macOS zsh shell. Paste a command with Command + V, then press Enter. Copy only the command, without a $ prompt. The prompt is the line where Terminal accepts your next command.

**Success check:** A Terminal window is open. Internet access is available; you can install apps on this Mac.

> Start with a currently supported macOS version. Check Homebrew’s requirements for your Mac; Intel support is more limited. Existing installations can skip completed steps after checking their versions.

## 2. Install Apple developer tools

These tools supply Git and the compiler used for syntax highlighting. Run the first command, complete the macOS Install dialog, and wait for it to finish before running the checks. The full Xcode app is not required.

**Terminal**

```sh
xcode-select --install
```

**Terminal: Check after the installer finishes**

```sh
xcode-select -p
cc --version
```

**Success check:** A developer-tools path and a compiler version appear. “Command line tools are already installed” means you can continue.

## 3. Install Homebrew

Homebrew installs command-line apps. The command below is from brew.sh. Read its prompts, press Enter when asked, and enter your Mac login password if requested. Password typing is invisible; this is normal.

**Terminal**

```sh
/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"
```

**Terminal: Check after completing Homebrew’s Next steps**

```sh
brew --version
```

**Success check:** The output starts with Homebrew and a version number. Follow every “Next steps” command printed by its installer; those make brew work in new Terminal windows.

> If brew is not found, return to the installer’s Next steps instead of reinstalling it. Apple Silicon commonly uses /opt/homebrew; Intel commonly uses /usr/local. Use the instructions printed for your own machine.

## 4. Install Neovim and the core tools

Install the editor, Git UI, file-search tools, Python, and parser builder. These are the apps the workbench uses. Wait until Homebrew returns to the Terminal prompt.

**Terminal**

```sh
brew install neovim git lazygit ripgrep fd python tree-sitter
```

**Terminal: Check the installed tools**

```sh
nvim --version
git --version
lazygit --version
rg --version
fd --version
python3 --version
tree-sitter --version
```

**Success check:** Neovim is 0.12 or newer, Python is 3.9 or newer, and tree-sitter is at least 0.26.1. Each other command prints a version instead of “command not found”.

> If Neovim was already installed but is too old, run brew upgrade neovim. Do the same for an outdated python or tree-sitter formula. You do not need to upgrade every app on the Mac.

## 5. Download and install the workbench

Neovim is the editor; this repository adds its interface and workflow. The commands create a Developer folder in your home directory, download the source, check dependencies, and install a separate workbench profile. No GitHub account is needed to download it.

**Terminal**

```sh
mkdir -p "$HOME/Developer"
cd "$HOME/Developer"
git clone https://github.com/ardanngrha/vimdesk.git
cd vimdesk
./install.sh doctor
./install.sh
```

**Success check:** The installer prints Installed, Backup, and Launch. Its default config is ~/.config/vimdesk and its launcher is ~/.local/bin/vimdesk. Your existing ~/.config/nvim is preserved.

> Doctor’s [--] next to a language server, codex, or claude is optional. Missing core tools or an unsupported Neovim version must be fixed first. If the checkout folder already exists, use the update instructions below; do not delete your existing folder.

## 6. Open a two-repo practice workspace

A repository (repo) is a project folder whose history is tracked with Git. From the vimdesk source folder, run the demo below. It creates a new temporary folder with backend and frontend Git repositories, then opens your installed workbench. Each repo has a small change to review.

**Terminal**

```sh
./scripts/demo.sh
```

**Success check:** Neovim opens and lazy.nvim may download plugins on its first run. Wait for downloads to finish. If the plugin window stays open after completion, press q to close it.

> The practice repositories are local only: no remote, GitHub login, push, or real project is involved. Their path is printed in Terminal and may be cleaned by macOS later. Keep important work in your own project folder.

## 7. Finish plugins and syntax highlighting

The following commands go inside Neovim, not Terminal. Press Esc first, type the command including its leading colon, then Enter. Restore the locked plugin versions and wait until it finishes. Quit with :qa, then run ./scripts/demo.sh again in Terminal to restart.

**Inside Neovim**

```vim
:Lazy restore
```

**Inside Neovim: After restarting Neovim**

```vim
:WorkbenchParsers
```

**Inside Neovim: Check the workbench**

```vim
:WorkbenchDoctor
```

**Success check:** Parser downloads and compilation complete, then source files gain syntax highlighting. :messages shows parser progress/errors. Doctor lists installed tools. Optional language servers can still be missing.

> Do not close Neovim while parsers are compiling. If installation fails, check internet, cc --version and tree-sitter --version in Terminal, then retry :WorkbenchParsers.

## 8. Try your first edit, review and quit

Press Space, release it, then g, then Shift + g. The Git sidebar should list backend and frontend. Click a repo, then a changed file to see Before / After. For editing, open a file from Files, press i to type, then Esc to return to Normal mode.

**Inside Neovim: Save the current file**

```vim
:w
```

**Inside Neovim: Quit all windows**

```vim
:qa
```

**Success check:** The file saves with :w. :qa exits when no changes are pending. If there are unsaved edits, save first or use Space q q for a confirmation prompt. Press u in Normal mode to undo; Ctrl + r redoes.

> Space shortcuts are sequential, not simultaneous. Ctrl means Control, not Command. Inside LazyGit, q exits that Git view; press ? there to see its own bindings.

## 9. Open your own projects

PATH is the list of folders Terminal searches for applications. Back in Terminal, add the launcher folder to PATH so vimdesk works by name. Run this once for the default macOS zsh shell. If you use another shell, add ~/.local/bin to that shell’s PATH instead.

**Terminal**

```sh
printf '\nexport PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"\n' >> "$HOME/.zshrc"
source "$HOME/.zshrc"
command -v vimdesk
```

**Terminal: Open a real parent folder**

```sh
vimdesk "$HOME/Developer"
```

**Success check:** command -v prints the launcher path. Neovim opens the selected parent folder. For your own workspace, replace the example path or drag a Finder folder into Terminal after typing vimdesk and a space.

> Open the parent of your Git repos to see them together. If you just want one repository, opening its folder works too. Language servers, AI and remote Git authentication are separate optional setup steps.

## Optional: language support and AI

For completion, diagnostics and formatting, install language servers from the source checkout:

```sh
cd "$HOME/Developer/vimdesk"
./scripts/dependencies.sh languages
```

This installs servers for Go, JavaScript/TypeScript/React, Rust and Python. Projects still need their own runtimes and dependencies. Use a project-compatible Go toolchain, a Rust toolchain with Clippy, Node.js for JS/TS, and the project’s Python/venv. Follow the project’s setup instructions; the workbench does not install project packages for you.

AI is optional. Install and authenticate [Codex CLI](https://github.com/openai/codex) or [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview) using their official guides. Save files, stage the changes, click Generate in Git, select an agent, and review the subject before clicking Commit. The staged diff is sent to the selected provider using your account. Normal usage limits/costs apply.

The practice repos have no remotes. For real projects, configure a remote and authenticate with that Git hosting provider before Push/Publish. Git commit identity and remote login are different settings. See [GitHub’s first-time Git setup](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/git-basics/set-up-git).

## If something goes wrong

- **brew: command not found:** Run the exact Next steps printed by the Homebrew installer, then reopen Terminal.
- **destination path already exists:** The source was already downloaded. Use cd "$HOME/Developer/vimdesk", then git pull --ff-only and ./install.sh. Back up local edits first.
- **vimdesk: command not found:** Use ~/.local/bin/vimdesk, or complete step 9 to add the launcher to PATH.
- **Cannot type / tidak bisa mengetik:** Press i to enter Insert mode. Press Esc to return to Normal mode before shortcuts or colon commands.
- **No completion / tidak ada completion:** LSP servers are optional. Install the relevant server and project runtime, open an actual source file, then run :checkhealth vim.lsp.
- **No author identity / identitas commit belum ada:** For your own repo, configure user.name and user.email following your Git provider’s guide. The demo supplies its own local fixture identity only.
